# PPG Contract Closure Matrix

> Version: V4.4, 2026-08-21.
> Status: fail-closed cross-contract index. The current final-audit verdict is `NOT_CLOSED`; no matrix assertion, historical PASS, RTL/TB source or earlier review conclusion is closure evidence. RTL and TB proof are separately tracked as `EVIDENCE_PENDING`.
> Scope: every active interface or semantic contract named in Section 2. Drafts, baselines, historical logs and existing RTL/TB are non-normative reference material.

## 1. Status and Notation

### 1.0 V4.4 Range and Version Baseline Record

V4.4 performs a source-only range and version baseline audit. It classifies all
375 workspace Markdown files without treating non-active material as evidence,
fixes C01-C25 to their complete relative paths, normalizes ambiguous current
header metadata, and records a 26-file manifest plus every current normative
dependency as Cxx, path, version and source-line entries. The V4.4 baseline
does not change ports, timing, lifecycle, product semantics or any nonzero
system-contract closure gate. `CONTRACT_CLOSED` therefore remains unavailable.

### 1.1 V4.2 Change Record (Historical)

V4.2 closes the specific D01 safety-gate endpoint defect found by the
independent reverse-port read. `peak_valley_config_valid` is now a formal
registered input in C20 and C23, with the existing C22 input, and the unique
chain is explicitly `unpacker -> AMI -> PWI -> C20/C22/C23`. A low gate permits
safe transaction consumption and drain only; it cannot advance formal cross,
peak/valley, 9-to-15 or fine-window state. This semantic repair does not reduce
any global ledger count: G-FP-01 through G-FP-07 remain incomplete until every
active port, pending, fault, parameter and CDC row has a source-line proof.

V4.2 retains the frozen D01 joint V4/V5 configuration architecture. ACTIVE V4
remains `[639:0]`; `ACTIVE_V5_DETECTION[383:0]` occupies joint payload
`[1023:640]`; all Top, wrapper, manager, unpacker and configuration-CDC
instances must use explicit `C_CONFIG_WIDTH=1024`. V4/V5 share one shadow, one
CDC and one atomic COMMIT; a legal joint COMMIT increments `config_epoch` once,
while any invalid V4/V5 field or non-zero V5 reserved bit preserves both ACTIVE
halves and the epoch. V5 schema `8'h05` is a contract binding outside payload.
The V5 reset profile and `peak_valley_config_valid` safety gate are authoritative
in C04 and are forwarded only through AMI -> PWI -> detector children.

The current system verdict remains `NOT_CLOSED`: the source-located ledgers below
are target artifacts only where every row is individually anchored. Grouped rows
and this change record never prove closure.

V4.2 retains the K01-K05 semantic repairs and directly reconciles the V4.0
audit contradiction: the Section 12 grouped summaries are not the complete
source-located G-FP-01 through G-FP-07 ledgers required for closure. They are
therefore recorded as incomplete rather than counted as zero. V4.2 also
repairs the reverse-port discrepancies discovered during the independent
source read: the Top's two nonexistent Scheduler ports, AMI's omitted
blocking-gate output, PWC's direct-child hierarchy wording, IDAC's omitted
generation-width parameter, and obsolete/non-normative dependency records.
The ledger is part of the normative cross-contract index and never replaces
individual formal port tables. RTL/TB/Top/physical-signoff proof remains
`EVIDENCE_PENDING` and never changes a contract-audit count.

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `CONTRACT_CLOSED` | The named contract rule has one implementation-ready definition with no known internal interface, lifecycle, ownership, CDC or connection conflict. |
| `EVIDENCE_PENDING` | A rule has a verified internal contract definition, but current RTL/TB/top evidence is absent or predates V2.0. It never overrides a system `NOT_CLOSED` audit verdict. |
| `NOT_CLOSED` | A product decision, port, width, owner, release path or semantic definition is missing or contradictory. |

All signals below are registered in the 2 MHz system domain unless the CDC table says otherwise. `ID` means the complete retained identity group:

```text
frame_id[C_FRAME_ID_WIDTH-1:0]
sample_index[C_SAMPLE_INDEX_WIDTH-1:0]
color_ir[0]
frame_type[1:0]
precision[0]
config_epoch[C_CONFIG_EPOCH_WIDTH-1:0]
coef_epoch[C_COEF_EPOCH_WIDTH-1:0]
dc_recovery_epoch[C_DC_RECOVERY_EPOCH_WIDTH-1:0]
amb_code_epoch[C_CODE_EPOCH_WIDTH-1:0]
dc_code_epoch[C_CODE_EPOCH_WIDTH-1:0]
run_generation[C_RUN_GENERATION_WIDTH-1:0]
```

`TXN_ID` is atomically held wherever a result, owner, completion, recovery cache or discard record is held. `FAULT_ID` is atomically held with every fault record and snapshot. `identity_valid=0` requires every applicable identity field to be zero, except that a generation-scoped discard keeps its target `run_generation` as a mandatory scope field even when its optional trigger identity is invalid.

### 1.1 Exact Identity-Group Expansion

`TXN_ID` is the complete retained transaction group. In every port table it
expands, with the stated signal prefix, to the exact individual ports
`<prefix>_frame_id[C_FRAME_ID_WIDTH-1:0]`,
`<prefix>_sample_index[C_SAMPLE_INDEX_WIDTH-1:0]`,
`<prefix>_color_ir`, `<prefix>_frame_type[1:0]`,
`<prefix>_precision`, `<prefix>_config_epoch[C_CONFIG_EPOCH_WIDTH-1:0]`,
`<prefix>_coef_epoch[C_COEF_EPOCH_WIDTH-1:0]`,
`<prefix>_dc_recovery_epoch[C_DC_RECOVERY_EPOCH_WIDTH-1:0]`,
`<prefix>_amb_code_epoch[C_CODE_EPOCH_WIDTH-1:0]`,
`<prefix>_dc_code_epoch[C_CODE_EPOCH_WIDTH-1:0]` and
`<prefix>_run_generation[C_RUN_GENERATION_WIDTH-1:0]`.

`FAULT_ID` is the first-fault identity that must be observable without
requiring a consumer to reconstruct a transaction. It expands to
`<prefix>_frame_id[C_FRAME_ID_WIDTH-1:0]`,
`<prefix>_sample_index[C_SAMPLE_INDEX_WIDTH-1:0]`, `<prefix>_color_ir`,
`<prefix>_frame_type[1:0]`, `<prefix>_precision` and
`<prefix>_run_generation[C_RUN_GENERATION_WIDTH-1:0]`. It is qualified by the
adjacent `<prefix>_identity_valid`; every `FAULT_ID` field is zero when that
bit is zero. A source may additionally retain `TXN_ID` locally, but it shall
not add an unlisted supervisor or Top fault-snapshot port.

The exact group names are fixed as follows: AMI uses
`o_measurement_result_discard_identity_valid` (always 1 with the event) plus
`o_measurement_result_discard_<TXN_ID>`,
`o_detection_discard_identity_valid` plus
`o_detection_discard_<TXN_ID>`, and `o_ami_fault_<FAULT_ID>`; PWI and its
children use `i_detection_discard_identity_valid` plus
`i_detection_discard_<TXN_ID>`; Scheduler and SSW use
`o_scheduler_fault_<FAULT_ID>` and `o_ssw_fault_<FAULT_ID>`; supervisor
inputs use `i_ami_fault_<FAULT_ID>`, `i_scheduler_fault_<FAULT_ID>` and
`i_ssw_fault_<FAULT_ID>`; its observation output uses
`o_system_fault_<FAULT_ID>`. For `*_detection_discard_*` and private
`*_datapath_discard_*` groups, `run_generation` is a mandatory flush-scope
field. When identity-valid is 0, every trigger transaction field except this
scope field and `sample_valid` is zero; `sample_valid` is zero. This expansion
is a formal port-name macro, not an implicit packed bus or a permission for
width conversion.

Unless a row states a stricter rule, every listed 2 MHz input is sampled only
on the registered receiving edge; every output resets to zero; every event is
one cycle and low during reset; every valid/ready payload is held unchanged
until its documented transfer or explicit discard; and every inactive identity field
is zero. These common reset and hold rules apply to each grouped port in this
matrix and the corresponding module port contract.

### 2.1 Authoritative Instance Hierarchy

| Parent | Direct child / contained owner | Contract owner | Boundary rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ppg_control_top` | ACTIVE control-plane wrapper, characterization CDC, Scheduler, AMI, SSW, dedicated fault/abort supervisor | C01 | The complete direct-child set. Top has no direct manager or AMI-internal child instance. |
| ACTIVE control-plane wrapper | config CDC bridge, manager, ACTIVE unpacker | C03 | The wrapper is manager's only parent and transparently forwards manager generation, stop episode, physical idle, digital empty and system-fault blocking signals. |
| AMI | Stage1 calibrator, Router/overlap, reconstructor, DC recovery, NORMAL fork, IDAC controller, PWI | C10/C11-C18 | AMI owns retained ADC result processing, private discard and the sole digital-empty aggregate. |
| PWI | FIR, baseline/cross, peak/valley, precision controller | C18-C23 | PWI owns detection-discard broadcast and detection-chain empty aggregation. |
| Supervisor | no fault-source child owner | C24 | It consumes registered AMI/Scheduler/SSW records and manager-originated episode state; it never replaces an owner or creates completion. |

### 2.2 Contract Closure Versus Evidence

`CONTRACT_CLOSED` means the complete active contract set has one internally
consistent definition for the named interface and behavior. `EVIDENCE_PENDING`
means RTL, TB, final Top, physical timing or signoff proof is still needed.
It does not reopen a closed interface. `PASS` requires current implementation
evidence and is not a contract status. The current status is `NOT_CLOSED` only
while a defect found by the final audit remains unresolved; this matrix moves
an item to `CONTRACT_CLOSED` only after its owner contract, every parent-side
port and every consumer-side port agree.

## 3. Module Parameter Total

All width parameters are `integer >= 1`; parameter equality is checked at elaboration by Top. `C_ADC_DRAIN_WATCHDOG_COUNTER_WIDTH >= $clog2(C_ADC_DRAIN_WATCHDOG_CYCLES + 1)` and `C_ADC_DRAIN_WATCHDOG_CYCLES >= 1` are mandatory. The fixed current values are `C_RUN_GENERATION_WIDTH=8`, `C_ADC_DRAIN_WATCHDOG_CYCLES=5000`, and `C_ADC_DRAIN_WATCHDOG_COUNTER_WIDTH=13`.

| Module / contract | Required parameters |
| --- | --- |
| Top | `C_CONFIG_WIDTH=1024`, `C_FRAME_ID_WIDTH=16`, `C_SAMPLE_INDEX_WIDTH=16`, `C_CONFIG_EPOCH_WIDTH=8`, `C_COEF_EPOCH_WIDTH=8`, `C_DC_RECOVERY_EPOCH_WIDTH=8`, `C_CODE_EPOCH_WIDTH=4`, `C_RUN_GENERATION_WIDTH=8`, `C_ENABLE_TEST_INJECTION=0`, watchdog parameters. |
| Manager | `C_CONFIG_WIDTH=1024`, `C_RUN_GENERATION_WIDTH=8`; it is the only state owner and output producer of `o_run_generation`, V4 ACTIVE, V5 ACTIVE and `config_epoch`. |
| Supervisor | all `ID` widths, `C_FAULT_CAUSE_WIDTH=8`, `C_FAULT_SOURCE_WIDTH=4`, `C_FAULT_SUMMARY_WIDTH=16`, watchdog parameters. |
| Scheduler, AMI, SSW | all `ID` widths; AMI also receives `C_ENABLE_TEST_INJECTION`. |
| AMI downstream data chain: Stage1 calibrator, calibrator-to-router boundary, Router/overlap, reconstructor, DC recovery, NORMAL fork and IDAC controller | all retained `ID` widths plus `C_RUN_GENERATION_WIDTH=8`; AMI passes the named Top parameter to each child and elaboration rejects a mismatch. |
| PWI and detector chain: PWI, FIR, baseline/cross, peak/valley and precision controller | all retained `ID` widths plus `C_RUN_GENERATION_WIDTH=8`; PWI passes the named parameter to each child and AMI/PWI elaboration rejects a mismatch. |
| ACTIVE mapping, unpacker and control-plane wrapper | `C_CONFIG_WIDTH=1024`; V4/V5 payload widths are fixed 640/384 and passed without conversion; neither generates a generation value. |
| TB contract | mirrors all Top parameters; it may override `C_ENABLE_TEST_INJECTION` only in verification builds. |

## 6. Owner, Pending and Release Table

| Pending owner | Establish | Hold | Normal release | STOP / abort / fault | Reset |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Scheduler waveform / ADC owner | Rule-A fire | owner ID and generation retained | matching AMI completion | existing cancellation or matching `success=0` controlled recovery; no direct clear | invalidate digital state only |
| AMI physical completion owner | accepted owner | real DONE/RAW/ID retained | production identity match | injected mismatch retains owner; STOP/abort replays original proven ID once with `success=0`; otherwise wait for legal real match or reset | invalidate, never fabricate completion |
| AMI pre-fork retained pipeline | accepted NORMAL result | full `TXN_ID`/generation and local buffers | accepted next pipeline stage | AMI private generation-scoped datapath-discard event flushes every local hold in that generation exactly once | clear, no discard event |
| AMI measurement fork | matched DC result | valid/payload/qualification ID | `valid && ready` | if unready, one explicit measurement discard record releases it | clear with no reset discard event |
| AMI detection fork | matched DC result | valid/payload/qualification ID | detection handoff | one explicit detection discard record releases it | clear with no reset discard event |
| AMI system-fault discard reason | supervisor one-cycle fault-discard event in the active generation | AMI-private `system_fault_discard_pending` | all current-generation terminal slots have transferred or emitted their exactly-once discard and AMI reports digital empty | it preserves `DISCARD_SYSTEM_FAULT` across later STOP/abort without re-emitting supervisor event | clear with no reset discard event |
| PWI/FIR/detector pending | local accepted detection transaction | local `TXN_ID`/generation | normal local pipeline consumption | unconditional generation-scoped discard broadcast clears every pending and run-scoped state of that generation at that edge | clear |
| Precision controller pending | accepted cross/return/window request | request `TXN_ID`/generation, window and switch state | normal safe commit/return | PWI current-generation discard flushes once; no direct STOP/abort clear port | clear |
| PWI precision fault hold | precision controller `o_mode_fault_event` | active fault ID/generation and safety gates | PWI sees controller active low after the same-generation AMI/PWI fault discard or reset | AMI alone promotes the record, supervisor creates abort/stop/fault-discard, then PWI discard releases controller state; no direct manager/supervisor route | clear |
| IDAC controller fault hold | IDAC controller rising blocking fault | active fault ID/generation and code-controller cause | source-specific safe cancellation leaves the source inactive; AMI observes the registered level | AMI alone promotes cause `8'h05`; STOP/abort cancel only local uncommitted IDAC work and never fabricate owner completion | clear |
| Supervisor first-fault snapshot | first blocking record | atomically held | never consumed by transaction flow | preserved through STOP/abort/recovery; later faults set summary only | clear only after safe recovery plus `diag_clear`, or reset |
| Watchdog drain episode | `o_stop_episode_active && !physical_idle` | counter and timeout latch | physical idle before boundary | one timeout record only; active fault waits for real idle or reset | clear |

## 7. Event, Fault Encoding and Recovery Table

### 7.1 Lifecycle event reasons

| Name | Value | Meaning |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `DISCARD_STOP` | `2'b00` | accepted external or system STOP lifecycle discard |
| `DISCARD_ABORT` | `2'b01` | registered abort lifecycle discard |
| `DISCARD_SYSTEM_FAULT` | `2'b10` | blocking-fault lifecycle discard; AMI retains the fault-discard reason internally from the single event until current-generation terminal drain, so later discardable work is not relabeled STOP/abort. |
| `DISCARD_RESERVED` | `2'b11` | never emitted; reset clears state without a discard event |

For either fork, a same-edge normal `valid && ready` transfer wins over discard. Otherwise priority is `SYSTEM_FAULT > ABORT > STOP`; reset dominates all events and emits no discard record.

`SYSTEM_FAULT` is selectable only from supervisor
`o_system_fault_discard_event`. A Top-registered external control abort selects
`ABORT`, emits a separate abort-drain stop request, and never creates a cause,
summary bit or first-fault snapshot without an independent blocking record.

### 7.2 Blocking cause and source codes

| Cause | 8-bit code | Source | Summary bit |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| none / reserved | `8'h00` | `4'h0` | none |
| AMI protected sample-index mismatch | `8'h01` | AMI=`4'h1` | 0 |
| AMI unrecoverable owner/protocol error | `8'h02` | AMI=`4'h1` | 1 |
| AMI unprovable recovery context | `8'h03` | AMI=`4'h1` | 2 |
| Precision-window switch timeout / precision blocking protocol fault | `8'h04` | AMI=`4'h1` | 7 |
| IDAC controller blocking fault | `8'h05` | AMI=`4'h1` | 8 |
| Scheduler unrecoverable protocol error | `8'h11` | Scheduler=`4'h2` | 3 |
| SSW identity/owner protocol error | `8'h21` | SSW=`4'h3` | 4 |
| SSW analog-safe protocol error | `8'h22` | SSW=`4'h3` | 5 |
| ADC physical-drain watchdog timeout | `8'h31` | Supervisor=`4'h4` | 6 |
| reserved | all other values | `4'h5`-`4'hF` | 9-15 reserved zero |

Waveform launch timeout and owner-deadline timeout remain local non-blocking historical diagnostics; they never drive a supervisor fault record. STOP discard drives only `o_result_discard_summary_sticky` and never a cause or summary bit.

### 7.3 Fault active recovery

| Source | `fault_active` deassertion condition |
| --- | --- |
| AMI mismatch / protocol | Original owner is legally released by matching normal completion or controlled original-ID `success=0` completion, and no AMI blocking cause remains. |
| AMI precision `8'h04` | The registered PWI precision-fault-active input is low after its same-generation AMI/PWI discard or reset; AMI then deasserts the contributed AMI active cause without releasing an ADC owner. |
| AMI IDAC `8'h05` | The registered IDAC controller blocking input is low after the controller's source-specific safe cancellation/recovery or reset; AMI then deasserts the contributed AMI active cause without releasing an ADC owner. |
| AMI record dispatcher | Each local cause retains an independent event-pending bit and captured `FAULT_ID`; `8'h01 > 8'h02 > 8'h03 > 8'h04 > 8'h05` dispatches one record per cycle until every pending cause has been reported. Dispatching a record does not clear its active lane. |
| Scheduler | Its documented unrecoverable protocol condition is reset or source-defined safe cancellation; non-blocking deadline diagnostics never assert `fault_active`. |
| SSW | Its documented safe waveform/owner recovery predicate is true and no SSW blocking cause remains. |
| Watchdog | Real `i_adc_physical_idle=1` is observed and the manager terminates the drain episode; reset always recovers. |
| Supervisor | `o_system_fault_blocking` deasserts on the next 2 MHz edge after all local active inputs are low and the watchdog recovery condition is true. Historical snapshot/summary remain until legal clear. |

## 8. Lifecycle and Same-Cycle Priority

| Scope | Priority, highest first | Required result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lifecycle manager | reset > Top-merged STOP (external STOP, supervisor stop or external-abort drain) > recovery action > START/COMMIT > status clear > transaction | STOP rejects simultaneous START/COMMIT/status-clear with existing conflict diagnostic; manager has no abort input. |
| Injection request slot | reset > STOP/system fault/abort terminal action > accepted existing owner completion > new identity/invalid request | A terminal event makes both ready outputs low; no request is accepted in that edge. |
| Fork slots | reset > normal transfer > system-fault discard > abort discard > STOP discard > hold | Reset has no event; every non-reset discard is exactly once. |
| AMI local fault dispatcher | reset > capture all rising lane events > dispatch one pending cause in `8'h01 > 8'h02 > 8'h03 > 8'h04 > 8'h05` order > source-specific active recovery | Every cause retains its own captured `FAULT_ID`; simultaneous PWI/IDAC faults generate two records, not one merged or lost record. |
| Supervisor diagnostics | reset > eligible new blocking fault > open-episode hold/recovery > episode close > legal diag clear | A new fault wins over close/clear. Close requires all local active levels low and watchdog recovery, preserves first-fault history, and re-arms exactly one event trio for a later episode. |
| Snapshot arbitration | watchdog > AMI identity/protocol > Scheduler > SSW; ties AMI > Scheduler > SSW | Later simultaneous faults set their summary bits only. |

`diag_clear` only clears historical diagnostics after all source active levels are low and recovery is complete. It never releases an owner, changes a normal result, cancels a pending injection or clears a run generation. START never clears first-fault history.

## 9. CDC and Reset Table

| Boundary | Fixed protocol | Reset rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ADC physical idle | one dedicated synchronizer before Top; Top sees a held 2 MHz level only | async assertion, synchronized 2 MHz release; low is the reset-safe value |
| Verification injection controls | one registered 2 MHz verification-control source; no mailbox exists inside Top or AMI | source holds valid/payload to ready; reset and inactive test-mode latch force ready low |
| Test-mode configuration | sampled only in CONFIG/READY, latched by accepted START, immutable in RUN | STOP/abort/reset clear the latch; accepted request still receives its terminal action |
| Diagnostic clear | one registered 2 MHz Top event distributed unchanged | reset clears event; manager status clear is a different local input |
| Fault records / abort / stop request / discard | all already registered 2 MHz point-to-point signals | reset clears pulse and held state; no asynchronous multi-bit sampling |

### 9.1 Reset, START, STOP, Abort, Fault and Clear Matrix

| Object | Reset | accepted START | STOP / abort / system fault | diagnostic clear |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Manager / wrapper | Clear lifecycle and generation to zero | Only manager accepts; increments generation once after blocking and drain predicates pass | Top-merged STOP starts one episode and blocks new work; abort is not a manager port | Manager local status clear only; system clear is not routed here. |
| AMI result/owner/forks | Clear state; no discard event | New-generation work only after manager permit | Formal result uses explicit discard; physical owner follows proven completion/recovery rules; internal detection state uses lifecycle discard | Clears historical local diagnostics only after safe recovery; never releases owner. |
| PWI and detector children | Clear pending/history | Accept same-generation normal work | Only AMI/PWI generation-scoped discard flushes active-generation state; no direct STOP/abort input | Clears historical diagnostics only. |
| Scheduler / SSW | Clear local digital state, no fabricated physical completion | Consume manager generation | Abort cancels uncommitted work; committed owner awaits matching completion/recovery; STOP blocks new work | Historical local diagnostics only. |
| Supervisor | Clear snapshot, summary, discard sticky, episode counter and pulses | Does not consume START | One fault episode emits exactly-once abort, stop request and fault-discard; watchdog watches manager episode only | Clear history only after all active faults recover. |

**9.2.5 Phase 4 boundary verification: does Phase 2's one-hop `assign`-chain detection miss
anything?**

Phase 2's "indirect read via `assign`" detection only follows one hop
(`assign wire=reg; <read wire in another domain's always block>`). Phase 4 built a
dedicated BFS-based checker (`cdc_phase4_multihop_assign_boundary_check.py`) rather than
assume the project's generally-direct coding style makes deeper chains moot. Real result:
multi-hop `assign` chains are **not** rare in this codebase — 181 (module, register)
pairs across 23 of the 24 scanned modules carry a chain of depth >= 2, up to 7 hops deep
(e.g. `ppg_sar9_sar15_safe_selection_wrapper`'s several sticky/fault registers). Tracing
every one of them: all terminate either back inside the same clock domain that wrote the
originating register (same-domain combinational re-composition) or at an output port
(the project's own registered-output-bridge convention, already known from Phase 2's own
docstring as a confirmed non-signal noise pattern). **0 of the 181 chains produce a
cross-domain read that Phase 2's one-hop detector would have missed** — verified by
running the real project through the checker, not assumed; the checker's own detection
logic is independently proven live (not vacuously passing on an empty dataset) via a
synthetic 2-hop cross-domain trap case in its own `--selftest` that the tool does
correctly flag. Full per-module chain-depth listing:
`ppg_system_integration/cross_reference_tools/cdc_phase4_multihop_boundary_report.md`.

boundary restatement, unchanged by this addition: not gate-level STA, not a tape-out
sign-off substitute).

## 10. Watchdog and `datapath_empty`

The supervisor begins a drain episode only after manager `o_stop_episode_active` proves an accepted external STOP, system STOP request or registered abort drain. Normal RUN ADC busy never starts the watchdog. On that acceptance edge the counter is zero. Thereafter each sampled 2 MHz cycle with `i_adc_physical_idle=0` increments it; `i_adc_physical_idle=1` wins at every boundary. The 5000th consecutive non-idle sample emits exactly one watchdog record. Repeated STOP cannot restart the episode. The watchdog never fabricates DONE, RAW, completion, idle or digital empty.

AMI alone computes `o_datapath_empty = 1` only after
`adc_chain_idle && normal_fork_idle && overlap_empty && reconstructor_empty &&
dc_recovery_empty && measurement_fork_empty && detection_fork_empty &&
pwi_fir_baseline_peak_valley_precision_empty &&
calibration_request_inflight==0`. PWI reports its empty one cycle after
consuming a detection discard. Physical ADC idle and IDAC idle are intentionally
outside this expression. Top and manager only consume AMI's output.

#### 12.4a V4.4 26-file Baseline Manifest

The 25 contract digests are full-file SHA-256 digests of their active paths.
The matrix row uses a deterministic self-normalized SHA-256: substitute the
64-hex digest field in the M01 row with the literal `<SELF_SHA256>` before
hashing the UTF-8 matrix file. A literal self-inclusive digest cannot be stable
because recording it changes the file being hashed. This is an integrity method,
not closure evidence; any later change to an active file invalidates this
baseline until the manifest is regenerated.

Each row anchors the owning formal table line; width, domain, reset, handshake and lifecycle wording are audited from that exact source row. | C11 | `ppg_system_integration/PPG_ADC_S1_PROGRAMMABLE_CALIBRATOR_CONTRACT.md:214` | note |  |  | **Cluster ⑥ finding, contract/RTL structural gap**: §6.1 (`:190-200`) requires `i_run_generation`, the full `i_datapath_discard_event/reason/identity_valid/<TXN_ID>` group, and `o_local_empty` to exist on this module ("端口仍必须存在" -- the port must still exist even if the implementation holds no output), and lists them again in the §6.1 port table (`:224-226`). The real RTL (`ppg_adc_s1_programmable_calibrator.v:58-116`) has **none of these 3 port groups** -- confirmed via full-file port-list read, 53 real ports, zero generation/discard/local-empty fields. Not treated as a functional deadlock: the module has 2 `always` blocks (a real held-output register, not purely combinational), but its sole upstream valid (`i_result_valid`) is already unconditionally gated by AMI's own `!flag_result_abort_discard` one hop upstream (at `ppg_adc_s1_redundancy_corrector.v`'s own `o_detect_valid` -> calibrator `i_result_valid` binding, `ppg_adc_measurement_idac_integration.v:1858`), so a STOP/abort/fault already prevents any new held value from entering this register without a dedicated generation-scoped discard port -- the contract's requirement appears to be over-specified for a module whose own valid is already externally gated, not a live bug. Recorded as a genuine contract/RTL structural mismatch, not silently fixed. **The identical gap recurs for `ppg_adc_programmable_reconstructor` (C14) and `ppg_adc_dc_recovery` (C15) below** -- same missing 3-port-group pattern, same contract-template language, same external-valid-gating mitigation; not re-derived in full for each, cross-referenced here once. |

| C10 | `ppg_system_integration/PPG_ADC_MEASUREMENT_AND_IDAC_INTEGRATION_WRAPPER_INTERFACE_CONTRACT.md:823` | note |  |  | **Cluster ⑥ finding, dangling output (whole-bus, likely oversight vs. intentional)**: `ppg_adc_result_router.v` has zero `always` blocks (pure combinational route-select, confirmed via full-file read: every output is a plain `assign o_X = i_X`, no registration). At AMI's instantiation (`ppg_adc_measurement_idac_integration.v:1938-1956`), **all 18 of router's shared-payload output ports are left empty** (`.o_calibrated_s1_value()` through `.o_dc_code_epoch()`), while its 3 branch-select valids (`o_amb_cal_valid`/`o_dc_cal_valid`/`o_normal_valid`) and `o_run_generation` ARE connected. This is not a functional bug: every downstream consumer (the NORMAL fork, and cross-cluster the IDAC controller for AMB/DCS) is wired directly to the **pre-router** wire (`dec_router_calibrated_s1_value` etc., the same wire that feeds router's own `i_calibrated_s1_value` input) rather than router's dangling output, which is bit-identical since router performs zero transformation on these fields -- confirmed at `ppg_normal_transaction_fork`'s own instantiation (`:1985`, `.i_calibrated_s1_value(dec_router_calibrated_s1_value)`, the identical wire router itself consumes). Router's own output ports for these 18 fields are therefore real, but functionally inert -- an intentional "skip the pass-through buffer" wiring optimization once verified, but recorded as a finding since it was not obviously reasoned from the port table alone. **Permanently dangling at the glue-top/DBG_OUT/P2S layer too, confirmed 2026-09-05 (P2 disposition pass)**: none of these 18 fields ever reach AMI's own top-level port list (C10) or `ppg_control_top.v`'s boundary -- they die at this AMI-internal instantiation, several hierarchy levels below Top -- so `PPG_CHIP_DIGITAL_TOP_SPI_P2S_INTEGRATION_CONTRACT.md` V1.5 §9 item 5's freeze on further `ppg_control_top.v` port/logic changes independently forecloses ever exposing them through the glue top, on top of the existing bypass already making them functionally moot. Not a TBD pending DBG_OUT design; not fixed (RTL unchanged). |

Two corrections to the prior 7-row content surfaced during this
re-verification: (1) the old row "C01 -> C03/C08/C09/C10/C24" was wrong to
include C03 -- `ppg_active_v4_control_plane_integration.v` (C03's RTL)
declares **zero** formal parameters (`grep -c "parameter" ppg_active_v4_control_plane_integration/ppg_active_v4_control_plane_integration.v` = 0), so its

the old row "C02 formal parameters" overstated C02's own parameter set as

the ID/epoch-width parameters belong to Top, Scheduler, SSW, AMI and

A system-wide finding that applies to every row below: **no producer or
consumer file in this cluster contains any synthesizable elaboration-time
parameter check** (`grep -n '\$error\|\$fatal\|initial\s*begin' ` returns
nothing in `ppg_control_top.v`, `ppg_400hz_frame_calibration_scheduler.v`,

`ppg_adc_measurement_idac_integration.v` or
`ppg_system_fault_abort_supervisor.v`). `ppg_control_top.v:288-292` documents
this as a deliberate choice ("综合RTL禁止使用initial块做运行时elaboration检查"
-- synthesizable RTL forbids `initial`-block runtime elaboration checks) and
records two width invariants as pure comments instead of assertions:
`C_CONFIG_WIDTH` must equal 1024 (ACTIVE wrapper's internal width is a fixed
literal, not a parameter) and `C_ADC_DRAIN_WATCHDOG_COUNTER_WIDTH` must be
large enough to hold `C_ADC_DRAIN_WATCHDOG_CYCLES` (currently 13 bits for
5000, i.e. 8192 > 5000, holds). Consistency elsewhere in this cluster is
enforced purely by identical default values across separately-declared
parameters of the same name -- there is no compiler-enforced guarantee if a
future edit changes one file's default without changing the others.

### 12.10 G-FP-06 CDC/reset/priority/clear ledger

| Boundary/event | Producer -> consumer | Domain/protocol | Reset/priority/clear | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| physical idle | ADC boundary -> C01 -> C08/C09/C10/C24 | dedicated sync to registered 2MHz level | reset-safe 0; never completion | C01:550-590; matrix 9. |
| characterization control | source -> C07 mailbox/synchronizer -> C01/C03/C02 | registered 2MHz held level/event | sync release; no duplicate manager sync | C07:94-105; C02:29-38. **Cluster ② real-evidence upgrade**: C07 instantiates its own dedicated `ppg_config_cdc_bridge` (`ppg_characterization_control_cdc.v:210-220`, `#(.C_CONFIG_WIDTH(3'd6))`) -- a second, independent bridge instance from the 1024-bit ACTIVE-payload one cluster ① already ledgered; same request-toggle/`ASYNC_REG` double-flop protocol, just a 6-bit `{static_characterization_enable, test_mux_ctrl[4:0]}` atomic payload (`:93,108`). Destination-side legality gate is C07's own, not the bridge's: `flag_destination_control_accept`/`flag_destination_control_reject` (`:109-110`) additionally require RUN-time mode-freeze agreement (`flag_destination_static_enable_match`, `:107`) before the bridge's arrival event is allowed to update the committed registers -- a bridge-plus-local-legality-gate pattern distinct from the ACTIVE-payload bridge, which has no local legality gate of its own (the manager does all its checking downstream, not the bridge's parent). |
| characterization-control source re-arm (priority nuance) | `ppg_characterization_control_cdc.v:81,196-206` (`reg_source_update_armed`) | source-domain `i_source_clk` registered handshake guard | source must de-assert `i_source_update_valid` before the mailbox re-arms for the next transaction (`:199-200`); a held-high `i_source_update_valid` across a completed handshake does **not** trigger a second send (`:201-202`) | `i_source_rstn=0` arms it (`:198`, so the very first request after reset is always accepted) | `ppg_characterization_control_cdc.v:196-206`. Cluster ② finding -- a source-side re-arm/anti-replay rule not covered by any existing G-FP-06 row (the ACTIVE-payload bridge has no equivalent explicit re-arm register; its busy/request-toggle comparison inherently serializes without needing one). |
| test injection | registered 2MHz source -> C01/C10 | valid/payload held to ready | reset/test-disabled ready 0; accepted request not revoked | C01:227-273; C10:11. |
| fault records/events | C08/C09/C10/C24 -> C24/C01/C02/C03 | registered point-to-point 2MHz | reset clears pulses; fault > close > clear | C24:30-57, 75-109; matrix 8-9. |
| discard | C10 -> C18/Top observer | one-cycle no-ready event | transfer > system-fault > abort > stop; reset no event | matrix 7.1, 8. |
| diagnostic clear | C01 registered `flag_diag_clear_event` -> all diagnostics | one 2MHz fanout | recovery required; never owner/fault/generation release | C01:726-764; matrix 9.1. |
| V4+V5 ACTIVE config snapshot transport | source_clk domain (SPI shadow) -> `ppg_config_cdc_bridge` request/ack toggle -> `i_clk` domain (`ppg_system_config_manager.v` `i_config_snapshot`/`i_config_update_event`) | request-toggle handshake, two independent `ASYNC_REG` double-flop synchronizers (source->dest request sync `ppg_config_cdc_bridge.v:163-179`; dest->source ack sync `:145-161`); one atomic `C_CONFIG_WIDTH=1024`-bit bus, busy-gated against mid-transfer overwrite (`:124-132,138-143`) | `i_source_rstn=0` clears source-side `reg_source_config`/`flag_source_request` (`:66,70,124-143`); `i_destination_rstn=0` clears `destination_config_o`/`destination_update_o`/`flag_request_sync*`/`flag_destination_ack` (`:76-79,86-87,101-120,164-190`); independent async resets per domain, no cross-domain reset sync needed since each side only samples its own registers | `ppg_config_cdc_bridge.v:70-190`. Cluster ① finding -- no prior row covered the ACTIVE-payload CDC boundary itself (existing rows cover physical idle, characterization control, test injection, fault, discard, diag clear only). |
| manager-local status clear (companion to diagnostic clear) | chip `i_diag_clear_event` -> `ppg_control_top.v` `flag_status_clear_event` (independent register, `:313,324-330`) -> ACTIVE wrapper `i_status_clear_event` -> manager `i_status_clear_event` | one 2MHz registered fanout, single consumer (manager only) -- a second, independent registration of the same source event that feeds `flag_diag_clear_event` | same single source as `flag_diag_clear_event` but a separate register; per the manager's own contract this input only clears `commit_ack_sticky`/`error_sticky` (W1C, `ppg_system_config_manager.v:657-659,671-673,685-687`) and never releases an owner, active fault, injection request or generation; `i_rstn=0` clears | `ppg_control_top.v:308-313,324-330`; `ppg_system_config_manager_semantic_contract.md:63`. Cluster ① finding -- the existing "diagnostic clear" row above documents only the AMI/Scheduler/SSW/supervisor-facing `flag_diag_clear_event` net, not this separate manager-facing net from the same source event. |
| amb-recheck-scheduler STOP/abort tie (priority nuance) | PWI-internal `flag_detection_discard_apply` -> **both** `ppg_amb_recheck_scheduler.v:61` (`i_stop_ack_event`) **and** `:62` (`i_control_abort_event`), the identical wire | one 2MHz registered signal wired to two formal ports of the same child instance | documented intentional tie, not a duplicate-port bug: PWI's own comment (`ppg_precision_window_integration.v:985-987`) states "AMI已经不再区分STOP与abort两种取消来源，二者统一折叠进这一根线路" (AMI no longer distinguishes STOP from abort as separate cancel sources for this scheduler); both collapse into `flag_control_cancel` (`ppg_amb_recheck_scheduler.v:174`) with identical effect, so priority between the two never has to be adjudicated inside this specific child | `ppg_precision_window_integration.v:980-987`. Cluster ③ finding -- no prior row documented this specific same-wire dual-port tie pattern (distinct from cluster ①'s manager-local-status-clear finding, which is a *separate register* fed by the same source, not literally the same wire on two ports). |
| C17 IDAC controller fault-bit clear ordering (priority nuance) | `flag_control_cancel = i_stop_ack_event \|\| i_control_abort_event \|\| !i_run_enable` (`ppg_idac_code_controller.v:580`) | one combinational OR gate, evaluated every 2MHz cycle | governs both pending-candidate release (G-FP-02 above) and, since the V2.3 fix, the three `CTX_*_FAULT_BIT` clears -- STOP, abort, and leaving RUN are treated identically here, but critically `i_start_ack_event` is explicitly *not* part of this cancel condition and must never clear an active/historical fault (contract §11.3, conformance ID IDC2-23) | `i_rstn=0` clears the whole packed context including these bits (`ppg_idac_code_controller.v:301` reset branch) | `ppg_idac_code_controller.v:26,580,1123-1124`. Cluster ③ finding, directly tied to the G-FP-03 deadlock-fix row above -- this is the priority rule whose earlier (backwards) implementation caused that real deadlock. |
| C20/C22 context-clear priority composition (priority nuance) | PWI generation-discard broadcast + lifecycle/reacquire/recheck events -> each detector's own `flag_context_clear`/`flag_control_clear` gate | one combinational OR composition per module, evaluated every 2MHz cycle, no CDC (same clock domain as the discard broadcast source) | C22's `flag_context_clear = i_start_ack_event \|\| flag_runtime_clear`, where `flag_runtime_clear = (i_detection_discard_event && generation match) \|\| i_recheck_accept_event \|\| !i_run_enable` (`ppg_peak_valley_window_detector.v:346-347`) -- i.e. a new START, a matching-generation discard, a real recheck takeover, and leaving RUN are all treated as equally-immediate full-context wipes, with no ordering between them since they OR into one flop-clearing condition; C20 mirrors this with its own `i_start_ack_event \|\| flag_control_clear \|\| flag_reacquire_clear` (`ppg_dynamic_baseline_cross_detector.v:577`), but additionally carries a **third, module-specific** immediate-clear source `flag_reacquire_clear = i_reacquire_request_event` (`:422`) that C22 does not have at the top-level context-clear gate (C22 instead takes `i_reacquire_active` as a level input elsewhere, not as an atomic context-clear pulse) -- a real asymmetry between the two sibling detectors' clear vocabularies, not a bug: baseline anchors must be atomically discarded the instant a reacquire is requested (stale slope/baseline data cannot survive a re-acquisition), while peak/valley candidates are already re-evaluated continuously and do not need a dedicated reacquire-triggered wipe | `i_rstn=0` clears the flop independent of this combinational gate (both modules) | `ppg_dynamic_baseline_cross_detector.v:421-422,577`; `ppg_peak_valley_window_detector.v:346-347,478-481`. Cluster ④ finding -- no prior row documented this specific composition or the cross-module asymmetry in what counts as an atomic context-wipe trigger. |
| C20/C22 protocol-sticky diagnostic clear (companion to diagnostic clear) | PWI's forwarded `i_diag_clear_event` -> each detector's own `protocol_error_sticky_o`/`o_protocol_error_sticky` flop (W1C) | one 2MHz registered fanout, per-module local sticky, independent of the AMI/Scheduler/SSW/supervisor-facing `flag_diag_clear_event` net documented in the existing "diagnostic clear" row above | set-over-clear priority in the same cycle: a fresh `flag_protocol_error_event` overrides a same-cycle `i_diag_clear_event` in both modules (C22 `:627-630`: the `flag_protocol_error_event` branch is checked *before* the `i_diag_clear_event` branch in the if/else-if chain, so a new violation wins); never releases an owner, pending event, or generation -- purely a diagnostic-history W1C, matching the manager-local-status-clear row's classification pattern | `i_rstn=0` clears (C22 `:626`; C20 `ppg_dynamic_baseline_cross_detector.v:566` mirrors the same shape) | `ppg_peak_valley_window_detector.v:623-633`; `ppg_dynamic_baseline_cross_detector.v:566`. Cluster ④ finding -- the existing "diagnostic clear" and "manager-local status clear" rows above do not cover either of these two module-local sticky flops. |
| C23 fault-hold clear-on-START re-evaluation (priority nuance, deliberate asymmetry vs. C17's IDAC fault) | `flag_lifecycle_cancel` (generation-discard-hit or leave-RUN) -> unconditional clear; else `i_start_ack_event` -> re-evaluate as `flag_blocking_protocol_fault` | one combinational if/else-if priority chain, evaluated every 2MHz cycle | `ppg_precision_window_controller.v:672-683`: `flag_fault_hold` (covers both switch-safe-commit timeout and illegal-START-config faults) clears unconditionally on `flag_lifecycle_cancel` (`:675-676`); if that is not asserted but `i_start_ack_event` is, the hold is **re-armed to `flag_blocking_protocol_fault`** rather than force-cleared (`:677-678`) -- i.e. a fresh START re-checks whether the *new* ACTIVE config is itself illegal and re-asserts the fault immediately if so. This is the **opposite** design choice from C17's IDAC search-exhaustion fault (G-FP-03 above, [[feedback-idac-fault-bit-stop-not-start-clears]]), where a fresh START must *never* clear a pre-existing fault -- but the two faults are semantically different classes: IDAC's is a hardware search failure that must survive until STOP/abort explicitly resolves it, while C23's is a switch-timeout-or-illegal-config condition that a fresh START is exactly the right moment to re-evaluate (the config may have been corrected before this new RUN). Documented here so the two are not mistaken for an inconsistency during future ledger review. | `i_rstn=0` clears (`:674`) | `ppg_precision_window_controller.v:672-683`. Cluster ⑤ finding. |
| C23 protocol-sticky clear-on-START (priority nuance, asymmetry vs. C20/C22's diag-clear-only pattern) | `i_start_ack_event` -> `protocol_error_sticky_o <= flag_protocol_error_event` (re-evaluate, not just clear); else `i_diag_clear_event` -> unconditional clear; else `flag_protocol_error_event` -> set | one combinational if/else-if priority chain per 2MHz cycle | `ppg_precision_window_controller.v:503-514`: unlike C20/C22's sticky (cleared only by `i_diag_clear_event` or reset, per the row above), C23's own `protocol_error_sticky_o` treats `i_start_ack_event` as a *first-priority* re-evaluation trigger (`:506-507`, "新RUN先清旧历史再记录当前配置错误" -- a new RUN first clears the old history, then immediately re-records if the new RUN's own config is itself illegal at that same edge), before falling through to the ordinary `i_diag_clear_event` W1C (`:508-509`) and then the ordinary set condition (`:510-511`). Consistent with the same fault-hold re-evaluation philosophy in the row above -- both of C23's own diagnostics treat START as a legitimate re-arm point, distinct from C20/C22's detectors which only ever clear their stickies via explicit diagnostic command. | `i_rstn=0` clears (`:505`) | `ppg_precision_window_controller.v:503-514`. Cluster ⑤ finding. |
| AMI integration-protocol sticky clear-over-set priority (priority nuance, third distinct pattern) | `i_start_ack_event \|\| i_diag_clear_event` -> unconditional clear; else the ~10-term protocol-violation OR -> set | one combinational if/else-if priority chain per 2MHz cycle | `ppg_adc_measurement_idac_integration.v:1168-1175`: unlike both prior patterns in this ledger -- C20/C22's clear-only-via-diag-event with **set-over-clear** same-cycle priority, and C23's **start-ack-first-then-re-evaluate** priority -- AMI's own `integration_protocol_error_sticky_o` gives **clear unconditional top priority** to either `i_start_ack_event` or `i_diag_clear_event` (`:1171-1172`, checked before the violation-set branch at `:1173`), so a violation occurring on the exact same cycle as a START or diag-clear is silently dropped rather than latched. This is a third distinct clear/set priority scheme among the sticky-diagnostic family already documented in this ledger (C20/C22 vs. C23 vs. this one) -- not a bug, but worth recording explicitly so a future reviewer does not assume all sticky diagnostics in this codebase share one convention. | `i_rstn=0` clears (`:1170`) | `ppg_adc_measurement_idac_integration.v:1168-1175`. Cluster ⑥ finding. |

### 12.12b Product-decision gate: SSW cause `8'h22` analog-safe convergence detector

**D03: `FROZEN` (2026-09-05).** Confirmed decision, recorded at
`PPG_SAR9_SAR15_SAFE_SELECTION_WRAPPER_INTERFACE_CONTRACT.md` Section 7.9a
(new subsection, original V1.4 changelog and Section 7.8 non-implementation
text preserved verbatim, not deleted): cause `8'h22` ("independent analog-safe
convergence detector", `PPG_SYSTEM_FAULT_ABORT_SUPERVISOR_INTERFACE_CONTRACT.md`
Section 3 fixed-encoding table) is **not applicable** to this chip's actual
analog implementation, closing the open item this matrix previously carried
in 12.12 item 2 as "a real product/design decision, not a documentation gap."

Evidence chain:

1. `i_analog_ready` -- a real chip-boundary analog-domain input port
   (`ppg_control_top.v:120`, "已同步模拟偏置/参考/输入选择RUN启动资格聚合结果，仅送
   wrapper") -- but it is a one-shot startup-eligibility level, not a signal
   that reports a time-varying convergence process.
2. `o_analog_safe` / downstream `i_analog_safe` -- despite the name, this is
   **not an analog signal**. SSW's own output
   (`ppg_sar9_sar15_safe_selection_wrapper.v:480`: `assign o_analog_safe =
   !(flag_red_wave_active || flag_ir_wave_active ||
   calibration_wave_active_o);`) is the inverse of SSW's own purely digital
   "is a RED/IR/calibration waveform currently being driven" state
   (`:400-402`, timing-window comparisons against `i_macro_tick` /
   `i_calibration_local_tick`), forwarded bit-identical to every consumer
   (C01/C03/C08/C23, per the existing Section 12.5 port rows). It carries no
   analog feedback.
3. This project's own analog designer confirmed the chip is a lab test chip
   (not a production part) with hard-wired bias circuitry: no charge-pump
   ramp-up, no slow bandgap-reference settling, and no calibration-loop
   convergence dynamics exist that would need an independent time-domain
   convergence check.

Conclusion: the physical phenomenon cause `8'h22` was meant to independently
verify -- analog convergence -- has no corresponding detectable signal in this
chip's real analog implementation. This is the same class of closure as D02
above (a confirmed, dated decision that permanently retires an open
product-decision gate), not a continued "definition not yet designed" gap.

**Scope of this decision:** D03 closes only the "does cause `8'h22` need an
implemented trigger condition" applicability gate. It does not add, remove or
renumber any `o_ssw_fault_cause` encoding (`8'h21` remains the only value SSW
actually emits); it does not touch any RTL; and it does not reopen or affect
any other G-FP-03 fault-source row.

>    `flag_commit_accept = (state_current == ST_CONFIG) && flag_snapshot_valid`,
>    so COMMIT (and therefore any change to this bit) is accepted only in the
>    CONFIG lifecycle state, never during RUN. The only path from RUN back to
>    CONFIG is STOP, and STOP itself already unconditionally clears the exact
>    in-flight state (C20's candidate context on `i_start_ack_event`; C22's
>    context on `i_run_enable == 1'b0`-driven `flag_runtime_clear`) that a
>    literal "toggle `config_valid` while a candidate stays mid-flight,
>    without touching STOP/START" scenario would need to observe. The literal
>    framing this note's 2026-09-05 predecessor called for is therefore not
>    constructible via real port-level drive without force -- a category
>    error created by the RTL's own COMMIT timing structure, not a gap this
>    session failed to fill. Same class of honestly-recorded construction
>    boundary as N08's pre-handoff facet and LFA-10(b).
>
> The real closure evidence instead covers the full acceptance intent (safe
> consumption/drain, zero new formal events, single reversible gate, no
> second producer) across all five real consumers via two complementary real
> constructions, both added to `tb_ppg_control_top_baseline_cross.v` V1.5
> (scenarios D01-01a/D01-01b, right after the existing N01/N08 scenario):

> with `peak_valley_config_valid=0`, drives 250 real RED transactions that
> would otherwise qualify for detection, confirms zero new formal events and
> C20/C22/C23 `o_local_empty` held 1 throughout (a background always-block
> invariant process, not a one-shot poll) with C23 never entering FINE, then
> restores `peak_valley_config_valid=1` and confirms the same curve
> immediately resumes producing a real PEAK -- proving reversibility and no
> second producer. Two real TB-only construction bugs were found and fixed
> along the way (a recommit attempted without STOPping first, rejected by the
> CONFIG-only COMMIT gate; and a snapshot race between C22's internal peak
> decision and the real `o_peak_valid && i_peak_ready` handshake a few cycles
> later) -- neither was an RTL defect; see the TB's own V1.5 changelog for the

> file's real `C_TARGET_RED_SAMPLES=700` scale plus the new scenario's own

>     proof remains `EVIDENCE_PENDING`"，但矩阵别处（当时的950行）已经有该ID的`CLOSED`断言，
>     脚本因此从未把这处过期文字标记出来，是本项目自己逐行读§12.13时才发现、按
>     `~~旧~~ **新**`修复的（见[[project-ppg-stage2-btagmissing-batch1-na-confirmations-20260910]]）。
>     和(d)不同：(d)是"同一行内多个状态词，脚本只取最左边一个"；(g)是"同一ID的不同物理行分别
>     判定，脚本把它们合并成一个OR，导致真正的单行过期文字被合并结果掩盖"——两者根因不同，不要
>     混为一谈。这个局限意味着`B_TAG_MISSING`/`A_CONSISTENT`分类下的ID，其矩阵里*每一处*提及都
>     可能仍需要人工确认是否过期，不能因为分类不是`E_STALE_MATRIX_TEXT`就假设该ID全文一致。

见Phase 5产出的memory `project-ppg-naming-governance-rule-20260906.md`。
